newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia c.bank sells HRK279 mln bills, rates flat.
newsitem.headline: Croatia c.bank sells HRK279 mln bills, rates flat.

text.p: Croatia's central bank sold 279 million kuna in 35- and 91-day bills on Wednesday, compared to only 22.5 million at last week's auction.
But a bank official put the net increase in volume at no more than 17 million kuna after most bill subscriptions were extended by banking investors upon expiry.
Issued rates were flat at 7.0 and 8.5 percent, repectively.

Participation at primary sales of the central bank paper is limited to Croatia's banking sector which uses these bills as collateral for Lombard loans, granted for a total of 12 working days each month.
It today issued 45 million kuna in new Lombard funds at 9.5 percent to help banks deal with an acute liquidity crisis, the official said.
The central bank has also been active in repurchasing its and treasury bills over the past week and injecting kuna to banks through five-day deals.
Last week it launched larger seasonal foreign exchange purchases that are used as a source of primary money creation. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
